Suggestion chips

Two to four suggested next prompts, as quiet buttons under a composer or an empty transcript.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • Under a composer after a turn ends, to offer the prompts most likely to come next.
  • Under an empty transcript, to show what can be asked of this repository or task.

When not to use it

  • For the view's actions, such as Start task or Stop. Use buttons.
  • For a choice among fixed options that stays selected. Use a select or radio inputs.
  • For an answer the agent is waiting on. Use an approval.
  • When there are no specific prompts to offer. Render nothing: a generic chip is worse than none.
  • For more than four. Pick the four most likely.

Accessibility

  • Use a ul with the class gw-suggestion-chips and an aria-label such as Suggested prompts, with one li per chip. A screen reader then announces the group and how many chips it holds.
  • Each chip is a button element with type="button" and the classes gw-button gw-suggestion-chips__chip. It is never a link and never primary.
  • The chip's text is the whole prompt it sends or places in the composer, specific to this conversation: Run the failing test again, not Tell me more. Do the same thing on every press, sending or filling, across the app.
  • A long prompt wraps inside its chip. Do not cut it short, because the text is what the reader agrees to send.
  • While a turn runs and a prompt cannot be sent, set the disabled attribute on every chip or remove the group.
  • Chips are 44px tall, and wrap onto further lines at phone width.
  • Tab moves through the chips in order. Enter and Space activate one. After a press, move focus to the composer or leave it on the transcript's new row. The component needs no script of its own.

Classes
